summary.one_liner: Netdata is an open-source, real-time infrastructure monitoring platform that collects per-second metrics, auto-discovers what it runs on, and provides dashboards, ML-based anomaly detection and alerting.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a monitoring agent that collects per-second metrics from systems, containers, VMs, hardware sensors, applications, logs and synthetic checks (APIs, TCP ports, ping, certificates). It auto-discovers most metrics with zero configuration and generates dashboards without a query language. It trains ML models per metric to detect anomalies and includes hundreds of built-in alerts, with notifications to email, Slack, Telegram, PagerDuty, Discord, Microsoft Teams and others. Metrics are stored in a tiered time-series database (per-second, per-minute, per-hour retention) and can be exported to Prometheus, InfluxDB, OpenTSDB, Graphite and others. Agents can stream to "Parent" nodes for centralized dashboards and retention, and an optional Netdata Cloud adds remote access, SSO and RBAC.
use_cases: infrastructure alerting to Slack or email
hardware sensor and disk health monitoring
how_to_run: Choose your platform and follow the install guide (Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, Windows, Docker, Kubernetes)
Access the Netdata UI in a browser at the agent's dashboard address (the README's exact URL is not shown in the extracted text)
Optionally configure collectors (see 'All collectors' and SNMP monitoring in the docs)
Optionally configure alert notifications (email requires a configured MTA by default)
Optionally configure Parents for centralized storage and dashboards
Optionally connect nodes to Netdata Cloud
notable: Per-metric ML anomaly detection trained at the edge
Tiered storage with roughly 0.5 bytes per sample and ZSTD compression
Parent-Child streaming for centralized dashboards and retention
Can run entirely in RAM (alloc or ram mode) with no disk writes
caveats: Netdata UI is closed-source (free to use), and Netdata Cloud is closed-source with free and paid tiers
Some hardware and sensor monitoring is only 'Full' on Linux; FreeBSD, macOS and Windows show 'Some' or limited support
OS services, network connections per PID and container monitoring are Linux-only per the platform table
OpenTelemetry support is described as coming soon
